name: EmoPhone: A Multi-Wave Dataset for In-the-Wild Mobile and Wearable Affect Sensing
description: This repository releases the raw data for D1, D2, and D3, three consecutive annual datasets collected as part of an in-the-wild affective sensing study from 2020 to 2022. Each dataset combines passive sensing from participants’ own Android smartphones and Fitbit wearables with dense in-situ affective state labels collected via the Experience Sampling Method (ESM). In total, the repository contains 53,139 ESM responses from 297 participants after quality control (328 participants recruited overall), captured in naturalistic daily-life settings. The dataset is intended to support research on moment-level affect prediction (e.g., valence, arousal, stress, and disturbance), personalized and cross-person generalization, cross-dataset transfer learning, and longitudinal analyses of behavioral and affective variability in mobile affective computing.

rai:dataLimitations:
This dataset consists of three annual, in-the-wild mobile and wearable affect sensing collections from a university-student cohort. As a result, its applicability is limited by several factors. First, the participant population is relatively narrow: participants were recruited from a university campus, are mostly young adults, and all used their own Android smartphones, so the dataset should not be treated as representative of the general population, iOS users, children, or older adults. Second, the three yearly datasets were collected under related but not identical protocols: wearable availability differed across years, some questionnaire content changed, and D3 introduced richer PANAS-style affect items. Third, missingness and partial coverage are unavoidable in real-world sensing because of non-response, device failures, syncing problems, and unequal wearable coverage. Some modalities were excluded from modeling because of low collection rates or known collection issues.

This dataset is intended for research benchmarking and method development. It is not recommended for clinical diagnosis, high-stakes mental-health screening, individual decision-making in employment or education, or any application requiring population-representative estimates or precise geolocation inference.
rai:dataBiases:
Several biases may affect this dataset. The dataset is subject to selection bias, because participation was voluntary and recruitment was conducted through a university-campus channel; the resulting cohort reflects a subset of Android-using university students rather than the broader public. The dataset also has demographic skew, especially toward young adults, and the gender balance varies across yearly collections. In addition, compliance bias may be present, because participants with lower response rates, missing wearable data, or insufficient smartphone coverage were excluded during quality control. This may bias the retained sample toward participants who were more compliant, more technically stable, or easier to monitor.

The labels are based on self-reported ESM responses, so they may also contain label bias arising from subjective interpretation, momentary self-assessment, survey interruption effects, or response fatigue. Finally, there is protocol and temporal bias across the three annual datasets: sensing coverage, wearable setup, and questionnaire design changed over time, and some collections overlapped with different pandemic-period conditions. These factors may affect model behavior and may lead to uneven performance across user groups, years, and collection conditions.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation:
This dataset contains personal and sensitive information. The applicable categories are:

-Gender
-Geography (location traces are present, although privacy-preserving transformations are applied)
-Age
-Health or medical data (e.g., psychological and mental-health-related questionnaire measures such as PSS-10, PHQ-9, and GHQ-12)

Others (please specify):
-smartphone interaction and behavioral traces (e.g., app/device usage events)
-wearable physiological and activity data (e.g., heart rate, step count, calories, distance)
-communication metadata and proximity/network traces (with privacy-preserving transformations such as hashing or identifier replacement)

The dataset does not explicitly include political or religious beliefs. It also does not explicitly provide a dedicated socioeconomic-status field in the released metadata. Personally identifiable fields were transformed before release using measures such as MD5 hashing of contact numbers, UUID replacement of MAC addresses, and random displacement of GPS longitude coordinates.
rai:dataUseCases:
This dataset is intended to represent moment-level affective and stress-related states in everyday life, as measured through repeated in-situ self-reports collected via the Experience Sampling Method (ESM), together with passive sensing from smartphones and wearables. The main target constructs include valence, arousal, stress, and task disturbance, with richer PANAS-style affect word intensities available in D3.

The dataset has been validated for research use cases such as:

-moment-level affect prediction from passive mobile and wearable sensing
-personalized / within-person affect modeling
-cross-user generalization benchmarking
-cross-dataset / cross-year transfer benchmarking
-longitudinal analysis of behavioral and affective variability

These use cases are supported by the collection design, shared label space across datasets, and baseline benchmarking reported for cross-dataset modeling. However, the dataset has not been validated for clinical diagnosis, medical decision support, automated triage, employee/student evaluation, or high-stakes individual-level interventions. Performance and fairness for populations outside the sampled cohort are also not established.
rai:dataSocialImpact:
Potential positive social impacts include enabling more realistic benchmarking for mobile affect sensing, improving methods for personalized and cross-user modeling, and supporting research on stress- and affect-aware systems in naturalistic settings. The dataset may also help the community study robustness, personalization, and generalization under real-world user heterogeneity.

Potential negative impacts include misuse for surveillance, emotion or stress inference without consent, or inappropriate deployment in contexts such as workplaces, schools, or insurance settings. Because the dataset is drawn from a relatively narrow cohort, models trained on it may perform unevenly across demographic groups, device contexts, or populations not represented in the study. There are also privacy risks inherent in behavioral, physiological, and location-related traces, even after de-identification.

To mitigate these risks, the dataset was collected under IRB approval, participants provided informed consent, participation was voluntary, privacy-preserving transformations were applied to sensitive fields, and the release is governed by access restrictions / usage terms for authorized research use. Users should not treat the dataset as evidence that models are safe or fair for high-stakes deployment.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: Data Collection
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: Participants were recruited from a university campus and attended an offline orientation session before data collection. They installed a custom Android data collection application, wore Fitbit devices throughout the study period. ESM prompts were delivered during waking hours (10 AM–10 PM) at random intervals, and participants completed repeated self-reports about affective state. The study team monitored uploads and participant compliance during collection.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: Annotation
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: Labels were provided directly by participants through ESM responses at each prompt. These labels include valence, arousal, stress, disturbance, and, in D3, PANAS-style affect word intensities. No third-party crowd annotators or synthetic annotators were used for the primary labels.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: Data Preprocessing
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: The raw files underwent structural validation and cleaning, including removal of incomplete rows, removal of invalid duplicate observations for time-based streams, sensor-specific outlier filtering, semantic consistency checks, and exclusion of low-coverage streams and participants that failed quality thresholds. Privacy-preserving transformations were applied before release, including hashing of contact numbers, UUID replacement of MAC addresses, and displacement of GPS longitude coordinates.
